correctness.rationale: The all-positive trace places queried edges inside exactly m fours; cycle obstructions force at most three edges per four, and at least m-1 saturated fours at size 3m-1 lock the remaining four, preventing one negative answer. An explicit 3m-2 support is shattered: binary positive cores need s_i tokens, each negative local token avoids its own bin, and two spare leaves are unrestricted. Hall holds whenever 2s_i <= sum(s_j)+epsilon_i; the only failures are (a) one full-star capacity 3 and both deficient capacities 1, or (b) one deficient capacity 3 and the other 1. Their explicit replacement blocks realize all constraints. Program independently replays all 2^13 labels at m=5 and direct partitions at m=2,3; finite checks are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The mathematical predicate is same-block equality with every block required to have size EXACTLY four and number of blocks unbounded. Full-text comparisons: unrestricted clustering (Bressan et al.), all-uniform triple partitions (published-finding corpus 165fac9), exact two-block partitions (published-finding corpus e71e3de), size-capped partitions (published-finding corpus 8b7b35), and refinement-closed partitions (published-finding corpus 2203ea). None implies the all-m size-four VC formula; two-block m=2 is acknowledged covered. Multiple specific published-finding corpus and primary searches found no exact all-m statement, but unindexed prior results remain possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible literature on exact equipartition pair-query VC dimension could prove an equivalent formula.
The Liu-Mukherjee conference paper was compared at abstract-level only; its formal objective is identification complexity, so a whole-document exclusion is not asserted.
Same-method proof and finite checks are not independent certification; exact m=2 base case already implied by existing two-block result.

value.rationale: Uniform block-size constraints obstruct the standard forest sufficiency argument. This theorem gives a sharp all-order capacity measure for pair-equality concepts when blocks all have size four; the positive construction uses an explicit Hall matching with precisely two structural exceptions. It fills a natural gap between the previously solved triple-uniform case and the weaker variable-size partition class, without claiming a general block-size theorem.
